2 SUDDAGUNTE PALYA POLICE STATION NOW NUMBERED AS C.C.NO.1446/2022 ON THE FILE OF THE HONBEL IV ADDITIONAL CHIEF METROPOLITAN MAGISTRATE BENGALURU AT ANNEXURE B AND C RESPECTIVELY AND ALL CONSEQUENTIAL PROCEEDINGS ARISING THERE FROM OFFENCES PUNISHABLE UNDER SECTIONS 34, 406, 420 OF IPC.
 -3-  NC: 2023:KHC:29403  CRL.P No. 4906 of 2023  THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR REPORTING SETTLEMENT,
THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioners-accused Nos.1, 2 to 5 are sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 34, 406, 420 of IPC.
2.
When the 2nd respondent approached M/s. Ace Venture Capitals, a loan consultants, for a loan of Rs.240 Crores on behalf of his company and had entered into a loan agreement dated 15.11.2021.

As per the mutual understanding, the petitioners had informed the complainant that, 3 months interest on the required loan amount will be Rs.3 Crores 60 Lakhs and that he needs to pay a sum of Rs.3.60 Crores as commitment amount in advance.
Thereafter, the accused after receiving the amount failed to transfer the loan amount and they are absconding.

3. The parties are present before this Court and they have filed a joint affidavit, stating that they have amicably settled the disputed among themselves and a sum of Rs.50,00,000/- will be paid to the 2nd respondent as full and final settlement of his claim and in lieu of the same, a sum of Rs.30,00,000/- through Demand Draft bearing No.004627 dated 20.06.2023 has already been received by the respondent No.2 and remaining Rs.20,00,000/- will be paid to one Mr.Adisheha V.,
on or before 1st seek of October 2023, and in lieu of the same, a cheque bearing No.000665 has been issued.
NC: 2023:KHC:29403 It is further stated that, the respondent No.2 has no objection for quashing the impugned proceedings.
4. Joint affidavit is placed on record.

5. Though the offences alleged against the petitioners- accused herein are cognizable and non-compoundable, however, having regard to the fact that the parties have amicably settled the dispute among themselves, it would be futile exercise, if the petitioners-accused are subjected to trial, since the probability of their conviction is remote and bleak in view of the settlement arrived between them.
Hence, the continuation of the criminal proceedings will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:

3 ORDER i) The criminal petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.1446/2022, on the file of the IV Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, stands quashed.
